chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid from Muhammad ibn Ali said:

I heard al-Rida (peace be upon him) saying: 'The slave is returned due to defects occurring within the year, from insanity, leprosy, vitiligo, and cataracts.' I said, 'And how is it returned from defects occurring within the year?' He said, 'This is the beginning of the year,' meaning Muharram. 'So when you buy a slave, if one of these characteristics occurs in him between you and Dhu al-Hijjah, you return him to his owner.'

key_terms.ذِي الْحِجَّةِ: Dhu al-Hijjah (the 12th month of the Islamic calendar)

ai.seo_question: What are the valid reasons and time period for returning a slave in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that 'one year' in this context refers to the lunar calendar year starting from Muharram, establishing a specific window for defect inspection (ayb) until Dhu al-Hijjah. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on transparency and fairness in commercial transactions, ensuring buyers are protected from latent defects that may not be immediately apparent.
